title: VVT Solenoid Bank 1 Intake (A) Open Circuit
shortDescription: Variable valve timing solenoid Bank 1 intake (a) circuit reports open circuit.
fullDescription:
This code sets when the PCM detects an abnormal electrical condition on the variable valve timing (VVT) oil control solenoid for Bank 1 intake (a). The solenoid uses pressurized engine oil to advance or retard the camshaft phaser, and its driver circuit is monitored continuously.

With the solenoid disabled the camshaft is locked at its mechanical default position, costing low-end torque, idle smoothness, and fuel economy. Sustained operation can also accelerate timing chain wear if oil pressure to the phaser is uncontrolled.
safetyImpact: Reduced power and rough idle; no immediate safety hazard.

causes.cause: Wiring harness damage at valve cover

fixSteps.title: Read freeze frame
fixSteps.instruction: Note RPM, load and oil temperature when fault was stored.

fixSteps.title: Measure solenoid resistance
fixSteps.instruction: Disconnect Bank 1 intake (a) solenoid and verify coil resistance per spec (typically 6-15 ohm).

fixSteps.title: Inspect harness and connector
fixSteps.instruction: Look for chafing near valve cover and oil contamination inside the connector.

fixSteps.title: Replace solenoid
fixSteps.instruction: Install new oil control valve and clear codes; retest.

faq.q: Will my engine be damaged if I keep driving?
faq.a: Short term no, but you will lose fuel economy and idle quality. Repair within a few hundred miles.
Yes - low or dirty oil starves the phaser; always verify oil level and quality first.

title: Camshaft Position A - Timing Over Advanced (Bank 1)
shortDescription: Bank 1 intake camshaft is more advanced than commanded.
fullDescription:
P0011 sets when the PCM commands the VVT phaser to a target position and the actual camshaft position reads more advanced than commanded by a calibrated threshold. Causes are usually mechanical: a stuck phaser, restricted oil control valve, or excessive timing chain stretch.

The code typically forces the engine into a default cam timing strategy, hurting power and economy. Continued driving with timing-chain wear can lead to chain failure and major engine damage.
safetyImpact: Possible engine damage if root cause is timing chain wear.

fixSteps.title: Inspect oil quality
fixSteps.instruction: Drain a sample - sludge plugs the OCV screen.

fixSteps.title: Clean / replace OCV
fixSteps.instruction: Remove and inspect the oil control valve screen for debris.

fixSteps.title: Measure cam phasing live
fixSteps.instruction: Compare commanded vs actual phase under load.

fixSteps.title: Check timing chain
fixSteps.instruction: Pull valve cover and inspect for slack or guide wear.

faq.q: Is this a chain or solenoid issue?
faq.a: Both are possible - mileage above 100k strongly suggests inspecting the chain.

faq.q: Why is rattle worst on cold start?
faq.a: Cold oil cannot pressurize the phaser quickly, allowing it to slap.

title: Camshaft Position A - Timing Over Retarded (Bank 1)
shortDescription: Bank 1 intake cam timing is more retarded than commanded.
fullDescription:
P0012 reports the actual camshaft phase is lagging the commanded value. The PCM expects the phaser to advance under load but it is not responding. Common causes include a phaser that cannot release oil, a failed solenoid, or low oil pressure.

Driveability symptoms are similar to P0011: lazy throttle response, MIL, and reduced economy. Severe phaser hardware failure may leave the cam stuck retarded permanently.
safetyImpact: Driveability degraded; no immediate safety risk.

fixSteps.title: Verify oil level/pressure
fixSteps.instruction: Check level then mechanical pressure if needed.

fixSteps.title: Test OCV operation
fixSteps.instruction: Bench-test solenoid with 12 V to verify spool moves freely.

fixSteps.title: Replace solenoid or phaser
fixSteps.instruction: Install correct part and torque to spec.

faq.a: Long-term yes - oil starvation that caused it can wear other components.

faq.q: Can I just clear the code?
faq.a: It will return; address the mechanical cause.

title: Camshaft Position B - Timing Over Advanced (Bank 1)
shortDescription: Bank 1 exhaust camshaft is over-advanced relative to commanded position.
fullDescription:
P0014 indicates the exhaust VVT phaser on Bank 1 is positioned more advanced than the commanded angle. On modern dual-VVT engines this affects EGR dilution and combustion stability.

Most causes are mechanical: stuck phaser, contaminated oil control valve, or chain wear. The PCM often disables VVT control until the fault clears.
safetyImpact: Reduced power and emissions performance; no immediate hazard.

fixSteps.instruction: Inspect for sludge and metal.

fixSteps.instruction: Use scanner to verify command vs actual.

faq.a: Yes - intake and exhaust phasers per bank.
Likely yes once readiness completes.

fullDescription:
P0015 sets when the exhaust phaser fails to advance to commanded angle. Causes mirror P0014 but in the opposite direction: stuck phaser, return spring failure, or oil starvation.

Driveability is mildly affected; long-term oil pressure issues should be ruled out.

title: Crankshaft / Camshaft Position Correlation (Bank 1 Sensor B)
shortDescription: Bank 1 exhaust cam position does not correlate to crank position.
fullDescription:
P0017 indicates the PCM compared crank and Bank 1 exhaust cam signals and found them outside the expected synchronization window. Mechanical timing slip, sensor fault, or reluctor wheel damage are common causes.

This is more serious than a simple solenoid code because it can mean the timing chain has jumped a tooth.
safetyImpact: Possible serious mechanical issue - inspect promptly.

fixSteps.instruction: Use scanner to view live correlation.

fixSteps.title: Inspect timing marks
fixSteps.instruction: Confirm chain alignment.

fixSteps.title: Replace chain/guides if worn
fixSteps.instruction: Full timing service.

faq.a: Limit driving - chain failure can bend valves.
Some manufacturers extended warranties on chain wear; check VIN.

The primary effect is loss of fueling precision and possibly turbo boost control issues.

title: Mass / Volume Air Flow B Circuit Low
shortDescription: Secondary MAF/MAP sensor B circuit voltage low.
fullDescription:
P00A2 sets when the PCM sees a voltage at or near ground from the secondary air flow sensor for longer than the calibrated time.

Usual causes are a shorted signal wire, a failed sensor, or a missing 5 V reference.

fixSteps.title: Verify 5 V reference
fixSteps.instruction: Sensor connector key on, engine off.

fixSteps.title: Check signal wire
fixSteps.instruction: Look for short to ground.

fixSteps.title: Replace sensor
fixSteps.instruction: If wiring is OK.

faq.q: How is this different from P00A1?
faq.a: P00A1 is performance, P00A2 is a low-voltage circuit fault.

faq.q: Can a wet sensor cause this?
faq.a: Yes - water intrusion is a common cause.

title: Mass / Volume Air Flow B Circuit High
shortDescription: Secondary MAF/MAP sensor B circuit voltage high.
fullDescription:
P00A3 sets when the secondary air flow sensor signal stays at or near reference voltage. The PCM cannot use the value for trim and reverts to default fueling.

Look for an open signal wire, missing sensor ground, or a failed sensor.

fixSteps.title: Verify ground
fixSteps.instruction: Continuity from sensor pin to PCM.

fixSteps.title: Inspect connector
fixSteps.instruction: Look for backed-out pins.

fixSteps.title: Replace sensor
fixSteps.instruction: If wiring tests good.

faq.a: The signal voltage is stuck near the 5 V reference instead of varying.
Open signal wire from a chafe or bad pin.
